slides.heading: The Skin
slides.body_md: Part 1 — the largest organ of the body.

visual.alt: Flow from the skin to protection, feeling and temperature regulation

slides.narration: The skin covers the whole body and is its largest organ. It is a waterproof wrapper that protects us, a sense organ that tells us about the world, and a thermostat that helps keep our temperature steady.

slides.heading: A vertical section of the skin
slides.body_md: Two main layers: the **epidermis** on top and the **dermis** below, over a **fat layer**.

slides.narration: The skin has two layers. The thin epidermis is the outer layer and has no blood vessels. The thick dermis below it holds blood vessels, nerve endings, glands and hair roots. Under the dermis lies a layer of fat.

slides.heading: The epidermis

rows: Dead, flat cells filled with keratin
Waterproof, protects against germs and wear; rubs off and is replaced
Makes new cells to replace the horny layer; contains melanin, the dark pigment that shields from sunlight

visual.alt: Table describing the horny layer and the Malpighian layer of the epidermis

slides.narration: The epidermis has two parts. The horny layer on the outside is made of dead cells filled with a tough protein called keratin. It is waterproof. Below it the Malpighian layer has living cells that divide to replace the dead ones, and it contains the pigment melanin.

slides.heading: The dermis

rows: Bring food and oxygen; carry heat; help control temperature
Sense touch, pain, pressure, heat and cold
Grow hair; the muscle makes the hair stand up

visual.alt: Table of the parts of the dermis with their position and job

slides.narration: The dermis holds many things. Blood vessels bring food and oxygen and carry heat. Nerve endings sense touch, pain and temperature. It has the sweat glands, the oil glands, the hair roots and tiny muscles that make hairs stand up. Fat cells below it store fat and keep us warm.

slides.heading: Functions of the skin

rows: Horny layer keeps out germs and water; melanin shields from sunlight
Nerve endings detect touch, pain, pressure, heat and cold
Sweating and changes in blood vessels keep the body at the right temperature
Sweat removes water, salts and a little urea
Sunlight on the skin helps to make vitamin D
The fat layer stores fat and reduces heat loss

visual.alt: Table of six functions of the skin and how each is carried out

slides.narration: The skin protects the body from germs, water loss and sunlight. It senses touch, pain and temperature. It helps to control body temperature. It removes some waste in sweat. In sunlight it helps to make vitamin D, and its fat layer stores food and keeps us warm.

slides.heading: Worked example 1: counting sweat glands
slides.body_md: A patch of palm skin is 2 cm by 3 cm and has 300 sweat glands on every square centimetre. How many sweat glands are on the patch?
bullets: Step 1: area = 2 × 3 = **6** square centimetres.
Step 3: so a small patch holds many glands, which is why the palms get damp when we are nervous or hot.

visual.alt: Worked table: six square centimetres and eighteen hundred sweat glands

slides.narration: First find the area by multiplying length by width. That gives six square centimetres. Then multiply by the number of glands in each square centimetre. The patch has one thousand eight hundred sweat glands.

slides.heading: The skin as a sense organ

rows: Nerve endings in the dermis, many in the fingertips and lips
Free nerve endings in the epidermis and dermis
Separate nerve endings that sense temperature

visual.alt: Table of sensations in the skin and the nerve endings that detect them

slides.narration: Nerve endings in the skin send messages to the brain. Some sense touch and pressure, and there are many in the fingertips. Others sense pain, and others sense heat or cold. This helps us avoid danger.

slides.heading: Derivatives of the skin

rows: Make sweat, which cools the body and removes some wastes
Make sebum, an oil that keeps skin and hair soft and waterproof
Protects the head, traps air to keep warm, and senses touch

visual.alt: Table of skin derivatives and the function of each

slides.narration: Some structures grow out of the skin. Sweat glands make sweat to cool the body. Sebaceous glands make oil that keeps skin and hair soft. Hair protects and keeps us warm. Nails protect the tips of the fingers. Mammary glands make milk for a baby.

slides.body_md: A doctor notes five problems. Name the skin derivative responsible for each.
bullets: Step 1: ask what each derivative does.
Step 2: match **dry, cracked skin and rough hair** with **sebaceous glands** (no oil).
Step 3: match **overheating in the sun** with **sweat glands**; **sore fingertips** with **nails**; a mother **unable to feed her baby** with **mammary glands**.

slides.heading: Hair and nails

rows: The shaft is dead; the root is living
The plate is dead; the root is living

visual.alt: Table comparing hair and nails in material, growth, living state and function

slides.narration: Hair and nails are both made of keratin, the same tough protein as the horny layer. The part you see is made of dead cells and grows from a living root under the skin. That is why cutting hair or nails does not hurt.

slides.heading: Summary
bullets: Epidermis: horny layer (dead, keratin) and Malpighian layer (living, melanin).
Dermis: blood vessels, nerve endings, sweat and sebaceous glands, hair follicles.
Functions: protection, sensation, temperature control, excretion, vitamin D.
Derivatives: sweat glands, sebaceous glands, hair, nails, mammary glands.

visual.alt: Summary table of the layers of the skin and what each contains

slides.narration: To recap. The epidermis has a dead horny layer and a living Malpighian layer with melanin. The dermis holds vessels, nerves, glands and follicles. The skin protects, senses, controls temperature and removes waste. Its derivatives are sweat glands, sebaceous glands, hair, nails and mammary glands.

slides.heading: Exam tips
bullets: In a skin diagram, label **horny layer, Malpighian layer, dermis, sweat gland, sebaceous gland, hair follicle, erector muscle, blood vessel** and **nerve ending**.
Say that the **horny layer is dead** and the **Malpighian layer is living**.
Give each derivative a **secretion or function**: **sweat, sebum, milk**.
Do not write that sweat glands lie in the epidermis; they lie in the **dermis**.
slides.narration: Exam tips. When you draw a section of the skin, label the layers and the glands. Say that the horny layer is dead and the Malpighian layer is living. Link each derivative to its secretion or function, and place the sweat glands in the dermis.

slides.heading: Keeping the Temperature Steady
slides.body_md: Part 2 — how the skin helps the body stay at about thirty-seven degrees.

visual.alt: Flow showing that on a hot day the body loses more heat and on a cold day less heat to stay at thirty-seven degrees

slides.narration: Whatever the weather, the temperature inside your body stays close to thirty-seven degrees. The skin does much of this work. On a hot day it helps the body lose more heat, and on a cold day it helps the body keep it.

slides.heading: Why a steady temperature matters

rows: Enzymes work best at this temperature
Reactions in cells slow down or go wrong
The brain, with the skin as the main organ of response

visual.alt: Table giving the normal body temperature and why it must stay steady

slides.narration: Enzymes in our cells work best at about thirty-seven degrees. If the body gets too hot or too cold, the reactions in the cells slow down or go wrong. So the brain checks the temperature and uses the skin to adjust heat loss.

slides.heading: Heat gain and heat loss

rows: Contact with cooler air and objects

visual.alt: Table of the sources of heat gain and the ways of heat loss

slides.narration: The body gains heat from respiration, from exercise and from warm surroundings. It loses heat by evaporation of sweat, by radiation from the skin, and by contact with cooler air. The skin can speed up or slow down this loss.

slides.narration: Sweat glands pour sweat on to the skin. When the sweat evaporates, it takes heat from the skin. This cools the body. On a damp day sweat dries slowly, so we feel hotter and stickier.

slides.heading: Worked example 1: heat lost by sweating
slides.body_md: A runner sweats 600 mL in an hour. Each millilitre that evaporates takes away about 2.4 kilojoules of heat. How much heat does the sweat carry away?
bullets: Step 1: sweat = 600 mL.
Step 2: heat lost = 600 × 2.4 = **1440 kilojoules**.
Step 3: this heat would otherwise raise the body temperature, so sweating is a very effective cooler.

slides.narration: Multiply the volume of sweat by the heat each millilitre takes away. Six hundred times two point four gives one thousand four hundred and forty kilojoules. That is a great deal of heat removed from the body.

slides.heading: A cold day: vasoconstriction

rows: Blood vessels of the skin narrow (vasoconstriction)
Less blood flows near the surface
The warm blood stays deeper in the body
Skin looks pale and feels cold
This is the sign of the reduced blood flow
Sweat glands make very little sweat

slides.narration: On a cold day the muscles in the vessel walls tighten and the vessels narrow. This is called vasoconstriction. Less blood flows near the surface, so less heat is lost. The skin looks pale and the fingers feel cold.

slides.narration: The opposite of vasodilation.

slides.heading: A cold day: other responses

rows: Erector muscles pull the hairs up
Raised hairs trap a layer of air, which is a poor conductor of heat
Muscles contract rapidly and release heat

visual.alt: Table of other responses to cold with how each helps

slides.narration: Other changes also help in the cold. Tiny muscles pull the hairs up, so they trap air that holds heat. We shiver, which makes the muscles release heat. The layer of fat under the skin also keeps heat in.

slides.heading: Worked example 2: reading the fingertip temperature
slides.body_md: A student puts a hand in cold air. The fingertip temperature is 32 degrees at the start, 27 after 5 minutes and 22 after 10 minutes. What happened to the skin and what is the mean fall each minute?
bullets: Step 1: fall = 32 − 22 = **10** degrees.
Step 2: mean fall = 10 ÷ 10 = **1** degree each minute.
Step 3: the fingertips cooled because the skin **blood vessels narrowed** (vasoconstriction), so less warm blood reached them.

slides.narration: Find the total fall by subtracting the last reading from the first. The temperature fell by ten degrees in ten minutes, so the mean fall is one degree every minute. The cause is vasoconstriction, which cuts the flow of warm blood to the fingertips.

sections.heading: 1. Structure and functions of the skin
sections.body_md:
The skin is the largest organ of the body. A vertical section shows two layers over a fat layer.

**Epidermis** (outer layer, no blood vessels)
- **Horny layer** (outermost): dead, flat cells filled with **keratin**; waterproof; protects against germs and wear; the cells rub off and are replaced.
- **Malpighian layer** (innermost): living cells that keep **dividing** to replace the horny layer; contains **melanin**, the dark pigment that shields the body from the harmful rays of sunlight and gives the skin its colour.

**Dermis** (inner, thick layer of connective tissue) contains **blood vessels**, **nerve endings** (touch, pain, pressure, heat and cold), **sweat glands**, **sebaceous glands**, **hair follicles** with their **erector muscles**, and, at its lower edge, **fat cells** that form a fat layer (subcutaneous fat) which stores fat and insulates.

**Functions of the skin**
1. **Protection** from germs, water loss, injury and sunlight.
2. **Sense organ**: touch, pain, pressure, heat and cold.
3. **Temperature control** (sweating and changes in blood vessels).
4. **Excretion**: sweat removes water, salts and a little urea.
5. **Vitamin D**: sunlight on the skin helps to make vitamin D.
6. **Storage and insulation**: fat in the fat layer.

Books vary in whether the fat layer is called part of the dermis or a separate layer (hypodermis), and in how many sub-layers of the epidermis they name; this chapter names the horny and Malpighian layers.

sections.heading: 2. Derivatives of the skin
sections.body_md:
**Derivatives** are structures that grow out of the skin.

| Derivative | Description | Function |
|---|---|---|
| **Sweat glands** | Coiled tubes in the dermis opening by pores | Make **sweat** (water, salts, a little urea); cool the body; excretion |
| **Sebaceous glands** | Small glands opening into hair follicles | Make **sebum**, an oil that keeps skin and hair soft and waterproof |
| **Hair** | Keratin shaft growing from a follicle | Protects, traps warm air, senses touch |
| **Nails** | Keratin plates on the fingers and toes | Protect the tips; help in picking up small objects |
| **Mammary glands** | Glands in the breast of a female | Make **milk** to feed the baby |

The visible shaft of a hair and the nail plate are dead; they grow from a living root, so cutting them does not hurt. The mammary glands are modified sweat glands in structure. The **erector muscle** attached to a hair follicle pulls the hair upright.

key_terms.definition_md: The watery liquid made by sweat glands, with salts and a little urea.
The oily secretion of the sebaceous glands.
The pit in the dermis from which a hair grows.

sections.heading: 3. Heat regulation: vasodilation and vasoconstriction
sections.body_md:
The temperature inside the body is kept at about **37 degrees Celsius** (about 98.6 degrees Fahrenheit), the temperature at which enzymes work best. The brain monitors it and the skin responds.

| | **Hot day** | **Cold day** |
|---|---|---|
| Skin blood vessels | **Widen** (**vasodilation**) | **Narrow** (**vasoconstriction**) |
| Blood near the surface | More | Less |
| Heat loss (radiation, contact) | More | Less |
| Sweating | Much; sweat **evaporates** and takes heat from the skin | Little |
| Hairs | Lie flat | Erector muscles pull them up; they trap air, a poor conductor of heat |
| Appearance | Skin red and warm | Skin pale and cold |
| Other | Heat loss by radiation | **Shivering** releases heat from muscles |

Heat is gained from respiration, exercise and a warm environment. Evaporation of 1 mL of sweat takes away about 2.4 kilojoules of heat (a commonly quoted value). In humans the erector muscles raise only small hairs, so this response is weak compared with that of furry mammals.

key_terms.definition_md: Widening of the blood vessels of the skin, so that more heat is lost.
Narrowing of the blood vessels of the skin, so that less heat is lost.
The change of sweat into vapour, which takes heat from the skin.

notes.exam_tips_md:
**Common mistakes**
- Swapping **vasodilation** and **vasoconstriction**, or the hot and cold days.
- Placing the **sweat glands in the epidermis**; they lie in the **dermis**.
- Saying the **horny layer is living**, or leaving out **keratin**.
- Writing that sweating cools the body, without saying that sweat **evaporates** and takes heat.
- Forgetting **melanin** in the Malpighian layer.

**How marks are usually awarded**
- 1 mark: a term, an odd one out **with its category**, a give-reason item.
- 2 marks: two functions or two points, matched.
- 3 marks: a three-row comparison (hot day and cold day) or three functions.
- 10-mark structured question: a short situation or diagram with parts of 2 to 4 marks; one part is a labelled diagram.

cards.back_md: Epidermis (outer) and dermis (inner).
The horny layer: dead cells with keratin.
The Malpighian layer: living cells that divide.
The dark pigment in the Malpighian layer that shields from sunlight.
A tough protein in the horny layer, hair and nails.

cards.front_md: Does the epidermis have blood vessels?
cards.back_md: No.
Blood vessels, nerve endings, glands, hair follicles, erector muscles.

cards.front_md: What does the fat layer do?
cards.back_md: Stores fat and insulates the body.

cards.front_md: Name six functions of the skin.
cards.back_md: Protection, sense organ, temperature control, excretion, vitamin D, storage and insulation.

cards.front_md: Which vitamin does sunlight help the skin to make?
cards.back_md: Vitamin D.
Water, salts and a little urea.
Make sweat, which cools the body and removes wastes.

cards.front_md: What is sebum and who makes it?
cards.back_md: An oil made by the sebaceous glands.
Keeps skin and hair soft and waterproof.
Protects, traps warm air, senses touch.
Protect the tips of fingers and toes.
Make milk to feed the baby.

cards.front_md: What is the erector muscle for?
cards.back_md: It pulls a hair upright.

cards.front_md: Why does cutting hair or nails not hurt?
cards.back_md: The shaft and the nail plate are dead; the living root is below the skin.
In the dermis; they open by pores on the surface.
About 37 degrees Celsius.

cards.front_md: Why must body temperature be steady?
cards.back_md: Enzymes work best at this temperature.
Widening of the blood vessels of the skin; more heat is lost.
Narrowing of the blood vessels of the skin; less heat is lost.

cards.front_md: Which of vasodilation and vasoconstriction happens on a hot day?
cards.back_md: Vasodilation.

cards.front_md: How does sweating cool the body?
cards.back_md: Sweat evaporates and takes heat from the skin.

cards.front_md: Why does the skin look red on a hot day?
cards.back_md: More blood flows near the surface.

cards.front_md: Why does the skin look pale on a cold day?
cards.back_md: Less blood flows near the surface.

cards.front_md: Why do hairs stand up in the cold?
cards.back_md: They trap a layer of air, a poor conductor of heat.
Muscles contract rapidly and release heat.

questions.stem_md: The dark pigment that protects the skin from sunlight is made in the Malpighian layer. It is called
questions.solution_md: Melanin shields the skin and gives it colour — option (a).

questions.stem_md: The outermost layer of the epidermis is made of dead cells filled with keratin. It is the
questions.solution_md: The horny layer is the dead, waterproof outer layer — option (b).

questions.stem_md: Sebum, an oily secretion that keeps skin and hair soft, is made by the
questions.solution_md: Sebaceous glands make sebum — option (a).

questions.stem_md: The widening of blood vessels in the skin on a hot day is called
questions.solution_md: Vasodilation means widening of the vessels — option (d).

questions.stem_md: The narrowing of blood vessels in the skin on a cold day is called
questions.solution_md: Vasoconstriction means narrowing of the vessels — option (d).

questions.stem_md: Sweating cools the body because

options.text_md: the sweat is colder than the body
the sweat widens the blood vessels
the sweat evaporates and takes heat from the skin
the sweat makes the hair stand up

questions.solution_md: Evaporation of sweat takes heat from the skin — option (c).

questions.stem_md: The horny layer of the epidermis is rubbed off every day, yet the skin does not wear away. This is because the layer below has living cells that
questions.solution_md: The Malpighian layer keeps dividing and renews the horny layer — option (d).

questions.stem_md: A farmer who works in the open for many months has darker skin than his sister who works indoors. The extra pigment is made by cells of the
questions.solution_md: Melanin is made in the Malpighian layer — option (b).

questions.stem_md: A paper cut that bleeds and hurts has cut through the epidermis into the
questions.solution_md: Blood vessels and nerve endings lie in the dermis — option (c).

questions.stem_md: A girl touches a hot pan and pulls her hand away at once. The heat was first detected by

options.text_md: the horny layer of the skin

questions.solution_md: Nerve endings in the skin sense heat and send messages to the brain — option (a).

questions.stem_md: A layer of fat below the dermis helps the body because it

options.text_md: insulates the body and stores food

questions.solution_md: Fat is a poor conductor of heat and is a store of food — option (b).

questions.stem_md: A child who is kept indoors all day lacks a vitamin that the skin makes in sunlight. The vitamin is
questions.solution_md: Sunlight helps the skin to make vitamin D — option (c).

questions.stem_md: In the figure of the skin, which letter marks the layer of living cells that keep dividing and hold the dark pigment?
questions.solution_md: B is the Malpighian layer; A is the horny layer, C a sebaceous gland, D a sweat gland and E a blood vessel — option (a).

questions.stem_md:
**Assertion (A):** The horny layer of the skin protects the body from germs.

**Reason (R):** The horny layer is made of dead cells filled with keratin and is waterproof.

Choose the correct option.

options.text_md: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution_md: Both are true, and the tough keratin-filled dead layer forms the barrier — option (c).

questions.stem_md: True or false? The epidermis contains many blood vessels.
questions.solution_md: False. Blood vessels are in the dermis; the epidermis has none.

questions.stem_md: Give the biological term: the tough protein found in the horny layer, hair and nails.

answer.model_answer_md: **Keratin.**

questions.solution_md: Keratin.

questions.stem_md: Choose the odd one out and name the category to which the other three belong: Epidermis, Dermis, Fat layer, Sebum.

answer.model_answer_md: **Sebum**; the others are **layers of the skin**.

questions.solution_md: Sebum is a secretion.

questions.stem_md: Give reason: the skin on the heel is thick and tough.

answer.model_answer_md: The **horny layer** of dead, keratin-filled cells becomes thick where the skin is **rubbed and pressed** the most, giving **protection**.

questions.solution_md: Thick horny layer protects.

questions.stem_md: A patch of skin on a sole is 4 cm by 2.5 cm and has 250 sweat glands on every square centimetre. How many sweat glands are on the patch?
questions.solution_md: Area = 4 × 2.5 = 10 square centimetres; glands = 10 × 250 = 2500.

questions.stem_md: Name the two layers of the epidermis and state which one is made of dead cells.

answer.model_answer_md: The epidermis has the **horny layer** (outer) and the **Malpighian layer** (inner). The **horny layer** is made of dead cells filled with keratin.

questions.solution_md: Horny layer and Malpighian layer; horny layer is dead.

questions.stem_md: Where is melanin made and what is its function?

answer.model_answer_md: Melanin is made in the **Malpighian layer** of the epidermis. It is a **dark pigment** that gives the skin its colour and **shields it from the harmful rays of sunlight**.

questions.solution_md: Malpighian layer; pigment that protects from sunlight.

questions.stem_md: Name two sensations detected by the skin and the part of the skin that detects them.

answer.model_answer_md: The skin detects **touch**, **pain**, **pressure**, **heat** and **cold** (any two). They are detected by **nerve endings** in the dermis (and the epidermis).

questions.solution_md: Two sensations; nerve endings.

questions.stem_md: State three functions of the skin.

answer.model_answer_md:
1. It **protects** the body from germs, water loss and sunlight.
2. It is a **sense organ**: nerve endings detect touch, pain, heat and cold.
3. It helps to **control body temperature** by sweating and by changes in its blood vessels. (Others: excretion in sweat; making vitamin D; storing fat.)

questions.solution_md: Any three functions.

questions.stem_md: Tabulate three differences between the horny layer and the Malpighian layer.

answer.model_answer_md:
| Horny layer | Malpighian layer |
|---|---|
| **Outermost** layer of the epidermis | **Innermost** layer of the epidermis |
| Made of **dead** cells | Made of **living** cells |
| Cells filled with **keratin** | Cells **divide** and hold **melanin** |

questions.solution_md: Position; living or dead; contents or function.

options.text_md: made of living cells of the dermis

questions.solution_md: The shaft of a hair is made of dead keratin cells — option (a).

questions.solution_md: Sebum is an oil that keeps the skin soft — option (b).

questions.solution_md: Sweat is mostly water with salts and a little urea — option (b).

questions.solution_md: A small erector muscle is attached to each hair follicle — option (c).

questions.stem_md:
**Assertion (A):** Nails protect the tips of the fingers and toes.

**Reason (R):** The nail plate is made of living cells with blood vessels.

Choose the correct option.

options.text_md: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution_md: The assertion is true. The reason is false: the nail plate is made of dead keratin cells, and only the root is living — option (a).

questions.stem_md:
**Assertion (A):** Sweating helps to cool the body.

**Reason (R):** Sweat contains water, salts and a little urea.

Choose the correct option.

options.text_md: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution_md: Both are true, but the composition of sweat does not explain the cooling, which is due to evaporation — option (d).

questions.stem_md: True or false? Sweat glands open on the skin surface through tiny pores.
questions.solution_md: True.

questions.stem_md: Give the biological term: structures such as hair and nails that grow out of the skin.

answer.model_answer_md: **Derivatives of the skin.**

questions.solution_md: Derivatives of the skin.

questions.stem_md: Choose the odd one out and name the category to which the other three belong: Hair, Nails, Sweat gland, Blood vessel.

answer.model_answer_md: **Blood vessel**; the others are **derivatives of the skin**.

questions.solution_md: A blood vessel is not a derivative.

questions.stem_md: Give reason: cutting the nails does not cause pain.

answer.model_answer_md: The visible nail plate is made of **dead cells** with no nerves; the living **root** is under the skin.

questions.solution_md: Nail plate is dead.

questions.stem_md: State one function each of (i) hair and (ii) nails.

answer.model_answer_md: (i) **Hair** protects the head from sun and cold by trapping warm air (and senses touch). (ii) **Nails** protect the tips of the fingers and toes.

questions.solution_md: Hair protects or keeps warm; nails protect the tips.

questions.stem_md: State the function of (i) the sebaceous glands and (ii) the mammary glands.

answer.model_answer_md: (i) The **sebaceous glands** make **sebum**, an oil that keeps the skin and hair soft and waterproof. (ii) The **mammary glands** make **milk** to feed the baby.

questions.solution_md: Sebum for soft skin; milk for the baby.

questions.stem_md: Name two substances present in sweat other than water and state one use of sweat to the body.

answer.model_answer_md: Sweat contains **salts** and a little **urea**. It **cools the body** when it evaporates (and removes small amounts of waste).

questions.solution_md: Salts and urea; cools the body.

questions.stem_md: Name three derivatives of the skin and state a function of each.

answer.model_answer_md: **Sweat glands** make sweat, which cools the body. **Sebaceous glands** make sebum, which keeps skin and hair soft. **Hair** protects and keeps the body warm. (Or **nails** protect the finger tips; **mammary glands** make milk.)

questions.solution_md: Three derivatives with a function each.

questions.stem_md: Tabulate three differences between sweat glands and sebaceous glands.

answer.model_answer_md:
| Sweat glands | Sebaceous glands |
|---|---|
| Make **sweat** (water, salts, urea) | Make **sebum** (oil) |
| **Coiled** tubes deep in the dermis, opening by a **pore** | Small glands that open into a **hair follicle** |
| **Cool** the body and remove some waste | Keep skin and hair **soft and waterproof** |

questions.solution_md: Secretion; structure and opening; function.

questions.stem_md: A girl has dry, cracked skin on her hands, and brittle nails, and finds that her scalp is oily. Name the derivative responsible for the oil and state its secretion and function.

answer.model_answer_md: The **sebaceous glands** are responsible. They secrete **sebum**, an oily substance that keeps the skin and hair **soft and waterproof**; if it is too much the scalp becomes oily, and if it is too little the skin becomes dry.

questions.solution_md: Sebaceous gland; sebum; keeps skin and hair soft.

narrowed, so more blood flows near the surface
widened, so less blood flows near the surface

questions.solution_md: Vasodilation brings more warm blood to the surface — option (a).

questions.stem_md: A man's hands turn pale and cold in a very cold room because the blood vessels of the skin have

narrowed, so more blood reaches the surface
widened and the sweat has evaporated
narrowed, so less blood reaches the surface

questions.solution_md: Vasoconstriction reduces blood flow near the surface and heat loss — option (d).

questions.stem_md: On a very humid day we feel hotter and stickier than on a dry day at the same temperature, because the sweat

options.text_md: evaporates quickly and cools us too much
makes the vessels of the skin narrow
evaporates slowly, so less heat is taken away

questions.solution_md: In humid air evaporation is slow, so cooling is poor — option (d).

questions.stem_md: A man standing in the cold begins to shiver. Shivering helps because the muscles
questions.solution_md: Rapid muscle contractions release heat — option (c).

questions.stem_md: In the cold, the hairs on the arm stand up and trap a layer of air. This helps because air is
questions.solution_md: A layer of trapped air insulates the skin — option (c).

questions.stem_md:
**Assertion (A):** On a cold day the blood vessels of the skin widen.

**Reason (R):** Narrowing of the skin vessels reduces the heat lost from the body.

Choose the correct option.

options.text_md: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution_md: The assertion is false: on a cold day the vessels narrow. The reason is true — option (b).

questions.stem_md: True or false? On a cold day the blood vessels of the skin widen.
questions.solution_md: False. They narrow (vasoconstriction), so less heat is lost.

questions.stem_md: True or false? Shivering releases heat because the muscles contract rapidly.
questions.solution_md: True.

questions.stem_md: Give reason: the face looks red after hard exercise.

answer.model_answer_md: The **blood vessels widen** (vasodilation), so **more blood flows near the surface** to lose heat.

questions.solution_md: Vasodilation.

questions.stem_md: Give reason: a person's skin looks pale and feels cold in very cold weather.

answer.model_answer_md: The **blood vessels narrow** (vasoconstriction), so **less blood flows near the surface** and less heat is lost.

questions.solution_md: Vasoconstriction.

questions.stem_md: The normal body temperature is 37 degrees Celsius. A patient's temperature is 39 degrees. By how many degrees is it above normal?
questions.solution_md: 39 − 37 = 2 degrees.

questions.stem_md: A boy sweats 20 mL an hour in a cool room and 120 mL an hour in a hot room. How many times more sweat does he make in the hot room?

Each millilitre of sweat that evaporates takes away about 2.4 kilojoules of heat. In the boy's case the extra sweat in the hot room is 100 mL an hour. How many kilojoules of extra heat does it carry away?
questions.solution_md: 100 × 2.4 = 240 kilojoules.

questions.stem_md: The skin of a boy's forehead is 33 degrees before a game and 36 degrees after 10 minutes of running. By how many degrees has it risen?
questions.solution_md: 36 − 33 = 3 degrees.

questions.stem_md: A blood vessel in the skin is 60 micrometres wide on a hot day and 20 micrometres wide on a cold day. How many times wider is it on the hot day?

Select the correct terms to fill in the blanks: [melanin, keratin, sebum, vasodilation, vasoconstriction, dermis, epidermis, sweat]

The horny layer is made of dead cells filled with (a) ______. The dark pigment (b) ______ is made in the Malpighian layer. The oily secretion of the sebaceous glands is (c) ______. On a hot day the skin blood vessels widen, a process called (d) ______. On a cold day they narrow, a process called (e) ______.
questions.solution_md: (a) keratin; (b) melanin; (c) sebum; (d) vasodilation; (e) vasoconstriction.

questions.stem_md: State what happens to the blood vessels of the skin on (i) a hot day and (ii) a cold day.

answer.model_answer_md: (i) On a hot day they **widen** (vasodilation), so more heat is lost. (ii) On a cold day they **narrow** (vasoconstriction), so less heat is lost.

questions.solution_md: Widen on a hot day; narrow on a cold day.

questions.stem_md: Explain how sweating helps to cool the body.

answer.model_answer_md: The sweat glands pour **sweat** on to the skin. When the sweat **evaporates**, it **takes heat** from the skin, so the body is cooled.

questions.solution_md: Sweat evaporates and takes heat.

marking_scheme.step: Sweat made and poured on to the skin
Evaporation takes heat from the body

questions.stem_md: State two responses of the body to cold, other than the narrowing of the blood vessels of the skin.

answer.model_answer_md: The **hairs stand up** and trap a layer of air, which is a poor conductor of heat. The body **shivers**, so the muscles contract and release heat.

questions.solution_md: Hairs erect; shivering.

marking_scheme.step: Hairs stand up and trap air

questions.stem_md: Why must the body temperature be kept almost steady at about 37 degrees Celsius?

answer.model_answer_md: The **enzymes** in the cells work best at about this temperature. If the body becomes **too hot or too cold**, the reactions in the cells slow down or go wrong.

questions.solution_md: Enzymes work best at this temperature.

marking_scheme.step: Enzymes work best at this temperature
Reactions go wrong if too hot or cold

questions.stem_md: Tabulate three differences between vasodilation and vasoconstriction.

answer.model_answer_md:
| Vasodilation | Vasoconstriction |
|---|---|
| Skin vessels **widen** | Skin vessels **narrow** |
| Occurs on a **hot** day | Occurs on a **cold** day |
| **More** blood near the surface, **more** heat lost | **Less** blood near the surface, **less** heat lost |

questions.solution_md: Vessel width; day; heat loss.

questions.stem_md: State three ways in which the skin helps the body to lose heat on a hot day.

answer.model_answer_md:
1. The blood vessels **widen** (vasodilation), so more blood flows near the surface and heat is lost by radiation.
2. The **sweat glands** make more sweat.
3. The sweat **evaporates** and takes heat from the skin.

questions.solution_md: Vasodilation; more sweat; evaporation.

questions.stem_md: Describe three changes that take place in the skin and the body of a person who stands in cold winds, and state the use of each.

answer.model_answer_md: The **blood vessels of the skin narrow** so less heat is lost. The **hairs stand up** and trap air that insulates the skin. The person **shivers**, and the muscles release heat.

questions.solution_md: Vasoconstriction; erect hairs; shivering.

questions.stem_md:
Study the diagram of a vertical section of the human skin. Parts are lettered A to E.

(a) Name the parts A, D and E. [3]

(b) Name the part B and state one of its functions. [2]

(c) Name the part C and state its secretion. [2]

(d) Draw a neat, labelled diagram of a hair with its follicle and erector muscle, naming three parts. [3]

answer.model_answer_md:
**(a)** A is the **horny layer**, D is a **sweat gland** and E is a **blood vessel**.

**(b)** B is the **Malpighian layer**; its cells **divide** to replace the horny layer (or it holds **melanin**, which shields the skin from sunlight).

**(c)** C is a **sebaceous gland**; it secretes **sebum**, an oil that keeps the skin and hair soft and waterproof.

**(d)** A **hair shaft** growing out of a **hair follicle** in the dermis, with an **erector muscle** attached to the follicle and a **bulb** at the base; three labels.

questions.solution_md: Horny layer, sweat gland, blood vessel; Malpighian layer and a function; sebaceous gland, sebum; labelled hair follicle.

questions.stem_md:
A patch of skin on a sole is 4 cm by 2.5 cm. It has 250 sweat glands on every square centimetre. A student also finds that the skin of the heel is much thicker than the skin of the arm.

(a) Calculate the number of sweat glands on the patch. [2]

(b) Name the layer of the skin that is thicker on the heel and give a reason for the thickness. [2]

(c) State the substances that the sweat contains besides water. [2]

(d) Draw a neat, labelled diagram of a sweat gland with its duct and pore, naming three parts. [4]

answer.model_answer_md:
**(a)** Area = 4 × 2.5 = 10 square centimetres; glands = 10 × 250 = **2500**.

**(b)** The **horny layer** of the epidermis; it is thicker where the skin is **rubbed and pressed** most, which gives **protection**.

**(c)** **Salts** and a little **urea**.

**(d)** A **coiled tube** in the dermis, a **duct** running up through the epidermis and a **pore** on the surface; three labels.

questions.solution_md: 2500 glands; horny layer, rubbing; salts and urea; labelled sweat gland.

questions.stem_md:
A mountaineer returns from a long trek. His lips and hands are dry and cracked, his nails are broken, his head is sunburnt where the hair is thin, and he notes that his sweat glands and sebaceous glands seem to be working differently.

(a) Name the gland that makes the oil that keeps skin soft and state the name of the oil. [2]

(b) State the function of (i) hair and (ii) nails. [2]

(c) Name the gland that makes milk and state in whom it works. [2]

(d) Draw a neat, labelled vertical section of the skin, naming four parts. [4]

answer.model_answer_md:
**(a)** The **sebaceous gland** makes **sebum**.

**(b)** (i) **Hair** protects the head from the sun and cold by trapping warm air. (ii) **Nails** protect the tips of the fingers and toes.

**(c)** The **mammary gland**; it works in a **mother** (female) to feed her baby.

**(d)** The **epidermis** (horny layer, Malpighian layer), **dermis** with a **sweat gland**, **hair follicle** and **blood vessel**, and the **fat layer**; four labels.

questions.solution_md: Sebaceous gland, sebum; hair, nails; mammary gland, mother; labelled skin.

questions.stem_md:
A cyclist rides for an hour in the midday sun and sweats 450 mL. Each millilitre of sweat that evaporates takes away about 2.4 kilojoules of heat. His face turns red and the skin of his arms feels warm.

(a) Calculate the heat taken away by the sweat in the hour. [2]

(b) Name the change in the blood vessels of the skin and explain how it helps. [2]

(c) State why the sweat must evaporate in order to cool the body. [2]

(d) Draw a neat, labelled diagram of a section of the skin on a hot day, showing a blood vessel, a sweat gland and a pore, with four labels. [4]

answer.model_answer_md:
**(a)** 450 × 2.4 = **1080 kilojoules**.

**(b)** **Vasodilation**: the vessels **widen**, so **more warm blood flows near the surface** and more heat is lost.

**(c)** Evaporation **takes heat from the skin**; sweat that only runs off the skin would not cool it.

**(d)** A **wide blood vessel** near the surface, a **sweat gland** with its **duct** and **pore** and **drops of sweat** on the surface; four labels.

questions.solution_md: 1080 kilojoules; vasodilation; evaporation takes heat; labelled hot-day skin.

Sweat that does not evaporate does not cool

questions.stem_md:
A mountaineer's toe has a temperature of 31 degrees when she steps into the snow. It is 25 degrees after 5 minutes and 19 degrees after 10 minutes. Her skin looks pale and her arm hairs stand up.

(a) Calculate the total fall in temperature and the mean fall each minute. [2]

(b) Name the change in the skin blood vessels and explain the pale colour. [2]

(c) State two ways in which the standing hairs and the shivering that follows help her. [2]

(d) Draw a neat, labelled diagram of a section of the skin on a cold day, showing a blood vessel, a hair and the erector muscle, with four labels. [4]

answer.model_answer_md:
**(a)** Fall = 31 − 19 = **12 degrees**; mean = 12 ÷ 10 = **1.2 degrees a minute**.

**(b)** **Vasoconstriction**: the vessels **narrow**, so **less blood flows near the surface**, which makes the skin look pale.

**(c)** The standing hairs **trap a layer of air**, a poor conductor of heat; shivering makes the muscles **release heat**.

**(d)** A **narrow blood vessel**, a **hair standing erect**, the **erector muscle** attached to the follicle, and the **epidermis** and **dermis**; four labels.

questions.solution_md: 12 degrees and 1.2 a minute; vasoconstriction, less blood at the surface; trapped air, shivering; labelled cold-day skin.

questions.stem_md:
A rare condition leaves a boy with almost no sweat glands. His parents find that he overheats quickly while playing and that his skin is dry.

(a) Explain why he overheats on a hot day. [2]

(b) State one precaution that would help to protect him. [2]

(c) Name one other response of the skin that still helps him lose heat and explain how. [2]

(d) Draw a neat, labelled vertical section of the skin, naming four parts. [4]

answer.model_answer_md:
**(a)** Without sweat glands he cannot **sweat**, so there is no cooling by **evaporation of sweat**, and heat builds up in the body.

**(b)** Any one: **stay in the shade**, **wear light, wet clothing**, **drink plenty of water** and rest, or use fans, so that heat can be lost by other means.

**(c)** **Vasodilation**: the blood vessels of the skin widen, so **more warm blood flows near the surface** and more heat is lost by radiation.

**(d)** The **epidermis** (horny layer, Malpighian layer), the **dermis** with a **blood vessel**, **hair follicle** and **sebaceous gland**, and the **fat layer**; four labels.

questions.solution_md: No sweat so no evaporative cooling; shade or wet clothing; vasodilation; labelled skin.

marking_scheme.step: More blood near the surface, more heat lost
